binders: A real-valued random variable X : Omega -> R.
An exponent p in (0, infinity], treated by separate cases 0 < p < infinity and p = infinity.
hypotheses: For the finite-exponent clause, 0 < p < infinity.
For the endpoint clause, p = infinity.
conclusions: If p = infinity, then ||X||_L-infinity = ess sup |X|.
definitions_and_conventions: E X is the expectation of X; in the measure-theoretic description supplied by the source, it is the Lebesgue integral of X on (Omega, Sigma, P).
The source's bracket-free convention makes E |X|^p mean E[|X|^p].
E |X|^p is called the p-th absolute moment of X.
For fixed p and (Omega, Sigma, P), the source defines Lp as the collection of random variables X with ||X||_Lp < infinity.
For p in [1, infinity], the source says this quantity is a norm and Lp is Banach; for p < 1, it says the triangle inequality fails and the quantity is not a norm.
implicit_context: The expectation and essential supremum are governed by the underlying probability space.
The displayed finite-p and infinity formulas define a quantity for a random variable before the following sentence restricts Lp-space membership to those with finite value.

details: Finite exponents are strictly positive: p belongs to (0, infinity).
The value p = infinity is included only through a separate essential-supremum definition.
The source does not define this Lp quantity at p = 0 in the selected passage.
The integrand is |X|^p, so signs of X are removed before taking expectation.
The outer exponent 1/p is applied after expectation.
The displayed quantity is introduced for a random variable X without a stated finite-moment hypothesis.
The subsequent definition of the space Lp selects exactly those X for which the displayed quantity is finite.
For p at least 1, including infinity, the source asserts norm and Banach-space structure.
For 0 < p < 1, the same formula is retained but the source explicitly says it is not a norm because the triangle inequality fails.

undebatable_constraints: The finite-p formula uses the absolute value |X| raised to p inside expectation.
The p-th root, expressed by the outer exponent 1/p, is part of the finite-p formula.
The finite-exponent domain is 0 < p < infinity, not merely p at least 1.
The p = infinity value is the essential supremum of |X|, not a substitution of infinity into the finite-p power formula.
The underlying probability space supplies the expectation and the measure-relative essential supremum.
Finiteness characterizes membership in the space Lp; the selected formula itself is presented before that finiteness restriction.
For 0 < p < 1 the source does not claim a norm: it explicitly records failure of the triangle inequality.

ambiguities.issue: The codomain of ||X||_Lp for an arbitrary random variable with an infinite absolute moment is not explicitly stated.
ambiguities.evidence: The source first displays the formula for a random variable X, then defines Lp by the additional condition ||X||_Lp < infinity.
ambiguities.impact: The layout strongly suggests an extended nonnegative value is allowed outside Lp, but the selected text does not explicitly declare an extended-real codomain.

ambiguities.issue: The selected passage does not state whether elements of Lp are literal random-variable functions or equivalence classes modulo almost-sure equality.
ambiguities.evidence: It calls Lp a vector space of random variables and later says ||.||_Lp is a norm, without mentioning the usual almost-sure quotient convention.
ambiguities.impact: On literal functions the displayed quantity is insensitive to changes on null sets and is only a seminorm; genuine norm definiteness requires the almost-sure identification or a corresponding extensional convention.

ambiguities.issue: No separate definition of essential supremum is supplied in the selected passage.
ambiguities.evidence: The endpoint display uses 'ess sup |X|' directly, with the probability space named in the immediately following sentence.
ambiguities.impact: The standard probability-measure-relative meaning is structurally indicated, but low-level conventions for the essential supremum are inherited rather than spelled out here.

contract_plain_english: On a probability space, for a real-valued random variable X and a strictly positive finite exponent p, the source defines the Lp quantity as the p-th root of the expectation of |X|^p. At p = infinity it instead uses the essential supremum of |X|. The space Lp contains the random variables for which this quantity is finite. The source calls the quantity a genuine norm only when p is at least 1; for 0 < p < 1 the same formula is used but the triangle inequality fails.
